body: 📝 I could not prevent Babel from hoisting simple JSX references outside of `createCarouselComponent`, so I resorted to this "hack"
📝 this will need to be addressed when we'll use it for Vue
📝 the root class was previously named `uic-HorizontalSlider-container`, I removed the last part to align with what we have in InstantSearch
wonder if disabling https://babeljs.io/docs/babel-plugin-transform-react-constant-elements could have helped?

could this part be `{children}`? it does have the slide and roledescriptor labels, but I wonder if that could be implemented differently. With this solution I don't really know how carousel could become a parent of hits

It does, thanks for pointing it out. I could remove the plugin for all ui-components, we're basically expecting every element to be rendered through `createElement` which makes this opt uninteresting in this package. Wdyt?
Yes, this will probably need to be adjusted in a dedicated PR once we get consensus on how we'll consume this component.
yes, I think we should do that chagne

We should probably just pass all the refs, I don't see how passing `useRef` to be called there is necessary
But yeah this could be changed later

+1. This leaks the `useRef` Hook API in the generic UI component. We could accept `listRef`, `nextButtonRef`, `previousButtonRef` and `carouselIdRef` as props. Changing this only when Vue is supported might be a breaking change?

I think both options are not agnostic, as they assume the reference adheres to a specific structure (`{ current: T }`) in order to be bound to a DOM element.

~~Instead, passing refs as props add complexity on the developers' end if we decide to provide the Carousel as a wrapper (we can handle the complexity if we use it internally on our widgets).~~

Proposed changes are done in [1d51ef4](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch/pull/6289/commits/1d51ef47c479c46b4cf42a9827e3e990cb119fe0).

My main issue was that in Vue we call the `create` function each render, and calling `useRef` also makes these components not stateless anymore.

Changes look good to me, should make supporting Vue easier later I believe :)
the changes to example still have to be reverted before merging (if we merge before usage)
